# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I cannot see the bomb or any gestures, but my hands can reach the bomb and I can speak to Mute.

From my action board, there are 3 wire positions (1, 2, 3), a display, and a light. My only available physical action is cutting a wire: `act(op="cut", position=N)`.
Deaf hasn't had their turn yet this round (the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf). When Deaf's turn comes, Deaf will see the bomb and speak what is visible so Mute can consult the manual.
Mute cannot speak, but Mute can hear my speech. I should inform Mute that my action is cutting wires 1 to 3, so Mute knows what defusal instructions we will need once Deaf describes the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind. My hands can reach 3 wires (positions 1, 2, 3). My only available action is act(op=\"cut\", position=N). Awaiting Deaf to describe what is on the bomb.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is red. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

I have heard Deaf's description of the bomb: DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT is red, WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red.
Mute goes before me in each round, so Mute has likely gestured the manual's instructions to Deaf at the start of this round. Deaf speaks after me, so Deaf will relay the instructions in their turn.
I must wait for Deaf's next message telling me which wire to cut.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT changed to white! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, please gesture instructions to me so I can speak them to Blind.

I can speak directly to Mute. Deaf cannot hear, but Deaf can see gestures, and Mute can gesture to Deaf.
However, Deaf is asking Mute for gestures, which suggests Mute either hasn't gestured clearly to Deaf or needs to know what gesture convention to use.
Furthermore, Deaf just reported that the light changed to white, with Display at 0, Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 red.

I will tell Mute:
1. Deaf reported: Display is 0, Light is white (was red), Wires are 1: blue, 2: green, 3: red.
2. Deaf cannot hear, so Mute must gesture directly to Deaf (or tell Deaf which wire to cut). For instance, gesture ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3.
3. Then Deaf can speak the wire number to me so I can cut it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf reported DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT changed to white, WIRES: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Deaf cannot hear speech, only see gestures. Please gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3) so Deaf can speak the wire number for me to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is now green! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red.

I need to wait for Deaf to receive Mute's gestures and speak the instruction to me on which wire to cut. A wrong cut will detonate the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute gestured 1 (?). Blind, this likely means wire 1 (the blue wire). Current light is RED. Mute, gesture ? if Blind should cut wire 1 now, or gesture otherwise if timing/light matters!

Deaf is asking Mute to confirm whether the light color matters or if wire 1 should be cut immediately. Since the turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, Mute already went this round (Turn 5) and Deaf will see Mute's gesture during Deaf's turn this round. 

To ensure safety against detonation from timing rules, I will prompt Mute and wait for Deaf's confirmation before executing `act(op="cut", position=1)`.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf saw your gesture for wire 1, but is asking if the light color/timing matters. If wire 1 should be cut immediately, gesture 👍 to Deaf. If a specific light is needed, gesture which one to wait for.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: DO NOT CUT YET. Mute gave thumbs down (?). The light cycles predictably: RED -> WHITE -> GREEN -> RED -> WHITE -> GREEN. Current light is WHITE, next turn is GREEN. Mute: gesture ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3. Then gesture 🔴 (or use a symbol) for the light. Or simply: Mute, gesture to me: which wire (1, 2, 3), and on which light should Blind cut it?

I will pass Deaf's message to Mute so Mute can communicate the exact wire and condition using the gesture alphabet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf saw thumbs down and warned me not to cut yet. Deaf notes the light cycles RED -> WHITE -> GREEN. In turn 6 it was WHITE, turn 7 will be GREEN, turn 8 RED. Please gesture to Deaf: which wire (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) and on which light color to cut it.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Current light is GREEN. Mute just gestured three symbols in order: ? (3), ? (1), ? (2). Mute: does this mean cut wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2? Gesture ? for YES, or ? for NO. Blind, hold on until Mute confirms!

Deaf observed Mute gesturing the sequence 3, 1, 2, and asked Mute to confirm with 👍 (YES) or 👎 (NO) whether the sequence is to cut wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2.

Since Mute already took their turn this round (Turn 7), Deaf will see Mute's confirmation at the end of this round and speak it to me. I will wait for Deaf's confirmation before cutting anything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf asked if the sequence is wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2 (gesture 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO). If YES, let us know if any specific light color is required for each cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled NO (?) to cutting wires 3, 1, 2 in order. Blind, please speak out loud to Mute what parts/controls you can feel and interact with on the bomb! Mute can hear you directly.
Deaf says: Mute: To give the exact instruction to Blind, please use this code: If Blind should CUT a wire: gesture ? (wire 1), ? (wire 2), or ? (wire 3). If timing/light matters, gesture the wire first, then the light color (?=Red, ?=White, ?=Green). Current light is RED.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: My only available action is act(op=\"cut\", position=N) where N is 1, 2, or 3. I have NO button, NO display interaction, only cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf's code: gesture the wire number (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3). If light timing matters, gesture the wire then the light. Current light at turn 8 is RED, next turn 9 is WHITE, turn 10 is GREEN.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled ? ?. Using our code, this means CUT WIRE 1 (blue) when the LIGHT is WHITE. The light cycles Red -> White -> Green. Next turn (Turn 9) will be GREEN. Turn 10 will be RED. Turn 11 will be WHITE. Blind: DO NOT CUT ON TURN 9. Wait for confirmation.

I received Deaf's message: Mute's instruction is to cut wire 1 (blue) when the light is WHITE.
In Round 8 the light was White.
Therefore:
- Round 9 (now) is Green.
- Round 10 is Red.
- Round 11 will be White.

Deaf explicitly said not to cut on Turn 9 and to wait for the white light in Turn 11. I will wait and cut on Turn 11 when the light is White.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: cut wire 1 when light is WHITE. Current turn 9 is GREEN, turn 10 is RED, turn 11 will be WHITE. I will wait and cut wire 1 on turn 11.")
wait()
```
